title: Brain Drain from Academia to Industry
bottleneck: Industry salaries and compute pull top researchers — especially in AI, biotech, and semiconductors — out of universities, hollowing out teaching, mentoring, and public-interest research. Academia cannot match compensation, and the outflow concentrates expertise inside a few firms. Universities lose mentors and public-interest researchers, weakening the pipeline that feeds industry itself.
why_it_blocks: The public research base loses the very people needed to train the next generation and provide independent oversight. Public-interest research and independent safety evaluation suffer most from the outflow.
current_state: Joint appointments and industry fellowships slow but do not reverse the flow; the compensation gap keeps widening. The long-term cost to the research ecosystem is diffuse and hard to measure, so it goes unaddressed.
